subject: Interim: investigation of elevated p99/p95 and request backlog (batching/queue suspected)
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elenatorres@healthlytics.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T02:14:00Z
Subject: Sudden spike in timeouts / p99s tonight

Ava,

We started seeing a sharp increase in timeouts on your hosted API around 21:50 UTC last night. Our telemetry shows p95 jumping from ~240ms to ~1.9s and p99 up to ~6s between 21:50–22:40 UTC; error rate for POST /v1/generate rose to ~4.8% (5xx). This coincides with a customer-facing campaign so traffic was ~3x baseline but not huge.

We pulled traces and are attaching a small subset (hlx_traces_20261117-22.json). We see long queuing before the first token back in many requests — requests are stuck in "waiting for batch" for multiple seconds. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side (batching config, rollout, autoscale)? This is causing failed inferences for our users.

We need an ETA on mitigation and whether you can prioritize HealthyLytics' traffic.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
HealthyLytics

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T03:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in timeouts / p99s tonight

Quick summary of findings from the first pass (logs & deploy history attached):

- Root-cause hypothesis: head-of-line blocking from continuous batching + increased queue depth. Around 2026-11-17T22:05 UTC we pushed a minor optimization to increase batching_window_ms from 20 -> 40 and bump max_batch_size from 64 -> 128 for a specific path to reduce token-level overhead. Under steady traffic that is fine, but with a 3x traffic burst it creates larger in-flight batches and longer tail queuing for small requests.

- Evidence: sampled request traces show many requests waiting 1–3s in queue before being processed. The runtime metrics show concurrency in GPU worker queues spiking with higher headroom but per-request latency growing. Heap of pending requests increased until autoscaler reacted ~+90s later.

Immediate mitigations I propose (ordered by speed / risk):
1) Reduce batching_window_ms back to 20 and cap max_batch_size to 64 for hosted API globally (fast config flip). (I can push this in 3–5m.)
2) Emergency passthrough for HealthyLytics (no batching on their tenant) while we stabilize (requires approval but is quick to enable).
3) Add a temporary dedicated routing rule to send HealthyLytics to spare capacity pool (costly, but lowest customer impact).

Longer term: add per-tenant adaptive batching and queue-priority so bursty tenants don't create head-of-line blocking. Also improve autoscaler sensitivity for queue depth rather than aggregate GPU utilization.

I'm attaching server_batch_config.diff and ops_snapshot_20261118.log with the exact deploy.

-Markus
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime

---
Attachment: server_batch_config.diff (text/plain)
Attachment: ops_snapshot_20261118.log (text/plain)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T03:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in timeouts / p99s tonight

I implemented mitigation 1 and 2 as an emergency rollback & tenant passthrough:

- Batching_window_ms reverted to 20ms and max_batch_size to 64 across the hosted pool at 03:05 UTC.
- Enabled tenant passthrough for HealthyLytics at 03:08 UTC which forces immediate processing (no batching).
- Scaled spare workers +20% for the next 30 minutes.

Observed effect: within ~90s p95 dropped from ~1.9s to ~340ms and p99 back to ~1.1s for HealthyLytics requests. Error rate fell to ~0.6%. We're keeping increased worker count for 30m while we monitor.

Notes: cost hit is ~+15% for that window; if they want dedicated capacity we'll need a commitment (see SUP-4521). Marissa, can you coordinate a quick customer note (I added a tentative runbook link below)?

Runbook: hipchat:ops-runbook/p95-p99-investigation
